transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, yes, thank you. Well, what finally scared me into coming in is... well, after I eat too much, I’ve been going into the bathroom and making myself throw up so I won’t gain weight. Which is honestly so difficult at work, you know? I work retail over at the department store at the mall, and the employee restrooms are just a nightmare lately. They switched the cleaning company back in October, and I swear the new people don't even mop the floors. I told my manager, Donna—she's been there almost as long as I have, we both started right out of high school, if you can believe that—I told her we need to call corporate about the state of those stalls. She never listens, though. 

But, um, anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right, the bathroom. I've been making myself sick in there, and at home, too. It's just... it's gotten to where it isn’t just a one-time mistake anymore, and I realized I really needed to see somebody about it.
Can you tell me more about the times you eat and then make yourself throw up—do you usually feel like you've eaten a large amount of food in a short time before purging?

Well, yes... it is a lot. Honestly, it’s much, much more than I’d ever put on a plate in front of anyone. It usually happens after my bridge night, or if I get stuck on a late shift at the store. I'll come home and just... eat everything. Leftover casserole, a whole batch of cookies I baked, crackers, bowls of ice cream, all in one sitting. 

Which reminds me, my bridge group has just gotten so stressful lately. Martha—she’s my partner, we’ve been playing together since our kids were in middle school—she insists on using this new bidding convention that I just cannot get the hang of. And she gets so snippy when I mess up! I brought those cookies I baked for the group, these lovely snickerdoodles I've been making for years, and she actually had the nerve to say they were too sweet. Can you imagine? I was so worked up I just brought the whole tin home. 

But, um... what was I saying? Oh, right, the food. Yes, I come home from things like that and just eat all of it, the cookies and the casserole and everything else, just so much food at once before I go to the bathroom.
During these times when you eat a large amount of food, do you feel like you can’t stop yourself or control how much you’re eating?

Yes, that's exactly it. Once I start during those times, it feels like I’m just... on automatic. I'll be standing there in the kitchen, thinking, "I really should stop before Arthur wakes up and notices," but my hand is just reaching for one more thing, and then another. 

Arthur's my husband, by the way. He’s a very sound sleeper, thank goodness, but he’s been having this terrible trouble with his hip lately, so sometimes he gets up in the night to take an aspirin. We finally got him an appointment with Dr. Evans—you know, the orthopedic specialist over on Elm Street? Getting an appointment there is like pulling teeth! I had to call their office three times just to get someone on the phone who wasn't a machine. And then the receptionist, I think her name was Brenda, she was just so short with me. I understand they're busy, but a little common courtesy goes a long way, don't you think? 

But, oh, I'm sorry, I'm wandering again. What did you ask me? Right, feeling out of control. Yes, it's like I just can't stop myself once I get going, even when I know I should.

Besides making yourself vomit, do you do anything else—like fasting, using laxatives or diuretics, or exercising a lot more than usual—to try to control your weight or get rid of the calories after these eating episodes?

No, no, I don't do anything like that. Just the... just the throwing up. I don't take any pills or try to starve myself, and I certainly don't exercise. Goodness, with my knees, just standing on the sales floor for six hours is workout enough! 

They actually tried to get me to work an eight-hour shift on Black Friday. I told Donna, "Donna, you know my knees can't take eight hours on that hard tile." And you know what she said? She told me I should invest in better shoes. As if a pair of Dr. Scholl's is going to fix thirty years of retail work! I was so mad, I went straight to the breakroom and had half a box of those stale donuts someone brought in. The breakroom is another thing—they took away our good coffee maker and replaced it with one of those pod machines. It makes the weakest coffee you've ever tasted, and the pods are so expensive. 

Anyway... what were we talking about? Oh, right, laxatives and things. No, I don't use any of those. Just what I told you before.
